# Service navigation

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use Service navigation beneath the GOV.UK header to show a service name and a small set of service-level navigation links.

## When to use

- Use for a GOV.UK service that needs a visible service name, service navigation links, or both beneath the GOV.UK header.
- Keep navigation short and limited to persistent top-level destinations supported by user research.

## When not to use

- Do not use to reproduce the GOV.UK global header or for page-level tabs and task navigation.
- Do not add a menu simply to fill the space when the service has no persistent top-level navigation.

## Anatomy

- **Service container (required):** A GOV.UK module and width container align the service bar with page content.
- **Service name:** A link identifies and returns to the service home page.
- **Navigation landmark:** A labelled nav contains a short list of service destinations.
- **Responsive menu toggle:** A hidden-by-default button controls the navigation list on narrow screens after enhancement.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Service name only | `div` | `govuk-service-navigation` | A service needs a clear name but no persistent navigation. |
| Service name and navigation | `nav` | `govuk-service-navigation__wrapper` | A service has a small set of persistent top-level destinations. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise govuk-service-navigation to reveal and operate the responsive menu toggle.
- Without JavaScript, navigation links remain visible and usable and the toggle remains hidden.
- Mark the current destination with the official current-item option and accessible current-page semantics.

## Accessibility contract

- Give the nav a concise aria-label that distinguishes it from other navigation landmarks.
- Give the toggle an aria-controls value matching the navigation list id.
- Do not communicate the current page through styling alone.

## Content rules

- Use the public service name consistently with the page title and service start page.
- Use concise nouns for destinations and avoid duplicating links already provided by the browser or page content.
- Do not include GOV.UK global navigation items in this service-level component.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.brand`
- `govuk.color.text`
- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`

## HTML examples

### Service navigation links

```html
<section class="govuk-service-navigation" aria-label="Service information" data-module="govuk-service-navigation">
  <div class="govuk-width-container"><div class="govuk-service-navigation__container">
    <span class="govuk-service-navigation__service-name"><a class="govuk-service-navigation__link" href="/">Example service</a></span>
    <nav aria-label="Menu" class="govuk-service-navigation__wrapper">
      <button type="button" class="govuk-service-navigation__toggle govuk-js-service-navigation-toggle" aria-controls="service-navigation" hidden aria-hidden="true">Menu</button>
      <ul class="govuk-service-navigation__list" id="service-navigation"><li class="govuk-service-navigation__item govuk-service-navigation__item--active"><a class="govuk-service-navigation__link" href="/account" aria-current="true"><strong class="govuk-service-navigation__active-fallback">Your account</strong></a></li></ul>
    </nav>
  </div></div>
</section>
```
